intro: Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan's statements on a new constitution, potential resignation, and peace talks with Azerbaijan dominate coverage across multiple outlets. Economic developments, including the 2027 budget draft and trade disputes with Russia, also feature prominently.

topics.title: Pashinyan links new constitution to peace deal and threatens snap elections
topics.text: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan stated that signing an agreement with Azerbaijan is necessary to make peace irreversible and outlined two paths for adopting a new constitution. He claimed he would resign regardless of a referendum outcome and threatened snap elections to push through the Azerbaijan-demanded constitutional changes. Pashinyan also reaffirmed his position on abandoning the Karabakh movement and said there are guarantees the peace agreement will be signed and ratified after the new constitution is adopted.

topics.title: Armenia considers legal action against Russian trade restrictions
topics.text: Armenian officials announced the country may appeal Russian trade curbs at the Eurasian Economic Union's court. The Economy Minister stated Armenia plans to sue Russia over the restrictions and confirmed he will not attend EAEU consultations in Moscow. Officials emphasized maintaining Armenia-Russia relations at the highest level despite the dispute.

topics.title: Government presents 2027 state budget draft with increased defense spending
topics.text: Armenia's parliament began discussing the 2027 state budget draft, which projects nominal GDP to reach 13.6 trillion drams, double the 2021 level. Defense spending is projected to rise by 53 billion drams in 2027. The Finance Minister highlighted reforms boosting capacity for capital expenditures and called for scrutiny of the widening gap between bank deposit and loan interest rates.

topics.title: Armenia deepens defense and economic ties with European partners
topics.text: Armenia and Germany discussed measures for economic diversification during the German Foreign Minister's visit to Yerevan. Defense cooperation was discussed with Sweden and India at the Brussels Security Conference. The Economy Minister denied intentions to replace the EAEU with the EU, emphasizing the need for quality products to export to European markets.

topics.title: Diaspora institutions honor benefactors and support education initiatives
topics.text: The Armenian Relief Society (ARS) unveiled a commemorative plaque honoring benefactor Hrayr Soghomonian. Camp Haiastan received an unprecedented $1.5 million gift from the Manguikian family. Glendale opened enrollment for the nation's first Western Armenian public school immersion program, while community leaders highlighted collective responsibility and the role of Armenian schools in national survival.

topics.title: ANCA endorsement logic explained in opinion pieces
topics.text: Multiple outlets published opinion pieces explaining the rationale behind Armenian National Committee of America (ANCA) candidate endorsements. The articles detail the logic and criteria used by the organization in selecting candidates to support.

topics.title: Armenian students win medals at International Astronomy Olympiad
topics.text: Armenian students secured six medals at the International Astronomy Olympiad. In chess, Haik Martirosyan defeated Richard Rapport in the Total Chess knockout stage.
